output.question: What is Amazon's stock split history?
output.answer: Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN) has split its stock four times. The most recent was a 20-for-1 split announced March 9, 2022. Shareholders of record on May 27, 2022 received 19 extra shares for each share, and the stock began trading on a split-adjusted basis on June 6, 2022. The three earlier splits were 2-for-1 on June 2, 1998, 3-for-1 on January 5, 1999 and 2-for-1 on September 2, 1999. Together the four splits mean one IPO share is now 240 shares (2×3×2×20). I found no source reporting any split after June 2022.

key_facts.fact: Trendlyne lists four AMZN splits: 20:1 on June 6, 2022; 2:1 on Sept 2, 1999; 3:1 on Jan 5, 1999; 2:1 on June 2, 1998.

The 20-for-1 split was announced after the market closed on March 9, 2022. Shareholders of record on May 27 received 19 additional shares per share, and split-adjusted trading began June 6, 2022. Shareholders had to approve it at the May 25, 2022 annual meeting.
First split: 2-for-1 on June 2, 1998, a little over a year after the May 15, 1997 IPO. Second: 3-for-1 on January 5, 1999. Third: 2-for-1 on September 2, 1999.

passages.quote: Amazon has split the face value 4 times since June 2, 1998.
each shareholder on record as of May 27 will have 19 additional shares
The stock price will begin trading on a split-adjusted basis on June 6.
Amazon’s first stock split took place on 2 June 1998, a little over a year after its 15 May 1997 IPO.
The second stock split was a three-for-one split and it took place on 5 January 1999.
Amazon’s third stock split was on 2 September 1999 and it was another two-for-one split.

caveats: I couldn't open Amazon's own sources. The IR FAQ page loaded without its answers, and the 2022 press release URL returned 404. All facts here come from secondary sources: Trendlyne, The Motley Fool and IG.
The 240-for-1 total is my own calculation from the four ratios (2×3×2×20). No page I opened states it.
No source I checked mentions a split after June 2022, but I didn't find a dated primary source confirming that nothing has happened up to November 2026.
The IG article has no publish date, and it covers only the 1998–1999 splits.
